newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sees $15.6 bln oil revenues in 96 - PdVSA.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sees $15.6 bln oil revenues in 96 - PdVSA.

text.p: Venezuela expects to receive $15.6 billion in revenues from oil exports in 1996, up from $14 billion last year, state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) President Luis Giusti said Thursday.
"We should reach at least $15.6 billion in revenues (from oil exports) this year," Giusti told a news conference before addressing a seminar in Caracas.
Exports account for the lion's share of PdVSA's total revenues.
Giusti said the improved revenues, are "the result of a higher price, but also of volume."
The price of Venezuela's basket of oil and crudes has averaged $17.19 per barrel for the year so far, compared to $14.84 per barrel last year.
Giusti estimated the average for 1996 as a whole would be around $16.50 per barrel, well above PdVSA's target of $13.50 per barrel at the start of the year.
Venezuela's oil production has reportedly risen to over three million barrels per day as the country flouts its Organization of Petroleum Exporting Country (OPEC) quota, oil traders have said.
The Venezuelan government has said it will use oil revenues that exceed their budgeted forecast to meet debt payments.
